subject: "Grandma, it's me": agree on a code word
preheader: A scam call that targets families, talking instead of typing, and dinner ideas.
intro: This week's scam is a nasty one, and the fix is a conversation you can have at the dinner table.

sections.label: Scam of the week
sections.title: The "Grandma, it's me" call
paragraphs: A caller says "Grandma, it's me" or "Dad, I'm in trouble." They need money fast and ask you not to tell anyone. Scammers can even imitate a voice.
bullets: Hang up and call the person on the number you already have for them.
Ask a question only they could answer, something you couldn't find online.
Agree on a family code word now, while things are calm. A person who is really in trouble can say it.

sections.label: Tip of the week
sections.title: Talk instead of type
paragraphs: Your phone can turn your voice into text, which is a gift if small keyboards drive you mad.
bullets: Open a message or note and tap the box so the keyboard appears.
Tap the little microphone on the keyboard.
Speak. Say "comma" or "period" for punctuation, then tap the microphone again to stop.

sections.label: AI trick of the week
sections.title: Dinner from what's in the fridge
paragraphs: Tell AI what you have, and it will suggest meals.
sections.prompt: I have chicken thighs, rice, carrots and half an onion. Give me 3 easy dinners that take under 40 minutes.
sections.note: Add anything you avoid, like "no dairy" or "low salt", and it will adjust.
